For the Petitioner : Mr. Arvind Kumar Choudhary, Advocate For the State : Mr. Vishwanath Roy,
Spl.P.P ------
Order No.04 Dated- 20.07.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with P.C.R. Case No. 324 of 2019 instituted under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per the complaint petition, the allegation is that the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the petitioner in the year 2009.

After two years of the marriage, the accused persons started demanding Rs. 2,00,000/- as additional dowry and due to non-fulfilment of the said demand, the accused persons tortured the complainant physically and mentally and ultimately she was ousted from her matrimonial house on 11.05.2019.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case with an ulterior motive in order to harass and blackmail him.
It is further submitted that there are major contradiction in the statement of the complainant in the written complaint, solemn affirmation as well as the statement of enquiry witnesses.

It is further submitted that the complainant did not want to reside in the joint family along with the old parents of the petitioner, therefore, the present false case has been lodged after ten years of marriage in order to pressurize the petitioner to live separately.

It is further submitted that petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case and will not indulge in Safran Khan @ Sarfan Khan vs The State Of Jharkhand on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146597331/
1 tampering with prosecution evidence and will abide by all terms and conditions imposed by this Court in the matter of granting anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Spl.P.P. appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
It appears that it is a complaint case lodged by the complainant and only summons have been issued against the petitioner as yet.
There is no necessity of custodial trial of the petitioner.
Hence, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, this anticipatory bail application is disposed off.

Petitioner is directed to seek regular bail before learned trial Court which shall be disposed off on its own merits in strict compliance with the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in 2021(10) SCC 773.
